final_proof:
Let X be the set of points, with |X|=v, and let ℬ be the collection of blocks, with |ℬ|=b. By the definition of a (nontrivial) BIBD, every block contains k points, every pair of distinct points is contained in exactly λ blocks, and 2 ≤ k < v with λ>0.

First determine the number of blocks containing any fixed point x. Let r_x denote that number. Count pairs (y,B) such that y is a point distinct from x and B is a block containing both x and y. Counting first by blocks through x gives r_x(k-1), because each such block contains exactly k-1 points other than x. Counting first by the choice of y gives λ(v-1), because there are v-1 choices for y and the pair {x,y} lies in exactly λ blocks. Hence

r_x(k-1)=λ(v-1).

Thus r_x is independent of x; denote its common value by r. Moreover,

r/λ=(v-1)/(k-1)>1,

where the strict inequality follows from k<v. Therefore r>λ.

Now form the v by b incidence matrix N, whose rows are indexed by the points and whose columns are indexed by the blocks, with N_{xB}=1 when x∈B and N_{xB}=0 otherwise. For points x and y, the (x,y)-entry of NN^T counts the blocks containing both x and y. It is r if x=y and λ if x≠y. Consequently,

NN^T=(r-λ)I_v+λJ_v,

where I_v is the v by v identity matrix and J_v is the v by v all-ones matrix. For every nonzero vector z∈R^v,

z^TNN^Tz=(r-λ)∑_{i=1}^v z_i^2+λ(∑_{i=1}^v z_i)^2>0,

because r-λ>0. Hence NN^T is nonsingular and has rank v. Since rank(NN^T)≤rank(N)≤b, it follows that v≤b. Therefore b≥v, as claimed.
